source_title: A visual circuit related to the parabrachial nucleus for the antipruritic effects of bright light treatment.
node_relevance_reason: Directly shows retina-recipient GABAergic vLGN/IGL neurons projecting to and inhibiting CaMKIIa+ neurons in the lateral parabrachial nucleus.
summary: Mouse study showing GABAergic vLGN/IGL neurons receiving RGC input inhibit CaMKIIa+ LPBN neurons; activating the vLGN/IGL-to-LPBN projection reduces itch-related behaviours, and the antipruritic effect of bright light depends on this pathway.
quotes: a subset of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) innervates GABAergic neurons in the ventral lateral geniculate nucleus and intergeniculate leaflet (vLGN/IGL), which subsequently inhibit CaMKIIα+ neurons in the LPBN.
Activation of both the vLGN/IGL-projecting RGCs and the vLGN/IGL-to-LPBN projections is sufficient to reduce itch-related behaviors induced by various pruritogens.

source_title: A Role for Thalamic Projection GABAergic Neurons in Circadian Responses to Light
node_relevance_reason: Sox14+ IGL/LGv GABAergic neurons are a vLGN/IGL projection class; efferent pattern described but LPBN not mentioned.
summary: Sox14+ IGL/LGv neurons project densely to superficial SC, sparsely to hypothalamus and contralateral LGN; no parabrachial target reported.
quotes: Notably, dense innervation was seen in the superficial gray and optic layers of the superior colliculus (SCs; Fig. 1M)

source_title: Enhancement and contextual modulation of visuospatial processing by thalamocollicular projections from ventral lateral geniculate nucleus
node_relevance_reason: Reviews vLGN as predominantly GABAergic with long-range inhibitory projections and cites anti-nociceptive effects via PAG, consistent with the node but not LPBN-specific.
summary: vLGN is mainly GABAergic and projects to SC, PAG, Re and lateral habenula; bright-light effects (antidepressant, anti-nociceptive, memory) act via distinct projection targets.
quotes: Unlike the dLGN, the vLGN is predominantly populated by GABAergic neurons [7][8][9] and does not project to the visual cortex 7 .

Consistent with this idea, vLGN neurons have been shown to be involved in bright lightdependent anti-depressive and anti-nociceptive effects and promotion of spatial memory via their projections to the lateral habenula, PAG and RE, respectively 11,12,17 .

source_title: Feature Detection by Retinal Ganglion Cells.
section: Downstream pathways and behavioral significance of retinal contrast detection.
node_relevance_reason: Describes sONa RGC input to GABAergic vLGN/IGL neurons projecting to lateral habenula, parallel to the node as a distinct vLGN/IGL output population.
summary: sONa RGCs drive two vLGN/IGL pathways: GABAergic neurons to LHb (antidepressant) and CaMKIIa neurons to nucleus reuniens; LPBN not mentioned.
quotes: First, sONα RGCs innervate GABAergic neurons in the vLGN and IGL that project to the lateral habenula (LHb) and mediate antidepressant effects of light (Huang et al. 2019).

source_title: Diverse GABAergic neurons organize into subtype-specific sublaminae in the ventral lateral geniculate nucleus
section: | Do laminated retinorecipient circuits organize visual pathways through the vLGN?
node_relevance_reason: Notes vLGN GABAergic subtypes likely include projection neurons with diverse targets, but subtype-specific projections are unresolved.
summary: vLGN neurons project to over a dozen subcortical regions; which GABAergic subtype projects where is not known.
quotes: Unfortunately, we do not yet have subtype specific resolution of vLGN projection neurons but hope that the data presented here will help to create a molecular toolkit for such circuit tracing in future studies.

source_title: Not a one-trick pony: Diverse connectivity and functions of the rodent lateral geniculate complex
node_relevance_reason: Reviews vLGNe/IGL efferents generally (SC, pretectum, pons, SCN) without parabrachial specificity.
summary: vLGNe and IGL have diverse subcortical efferents, none cortical; targets include SC, pretectal nuclei, zona incerta and pontine nuclei.
quotes: Importantly, neither vLGNe nor IGL project efferents to visual cortex or any other cortical region (Harrington, 1997).

Other regions associated with eye movements, visuomotor function, and attention innervated by vLGNe and IGL include two of the accessory optic system nuclei (lateral terminal nucleus and medial terminal nucleus; Swanson et al., 1974;Ribak & Peters, 1975), zona incerta (Brauer & Schober, 1982), and nuclei within the pons (Harrington, 1997).
